# Bonsai: full reference for LLMs

Bonsai (`bonsai-js` on npm) is a small, total, typed expression language for JavaScript. It evaluates untrusted expression text against host data without executing JavaScript. Every expression terminates: there are no loops, recursion, or assignment. An expression reaches host code only through functions the host declared and data the host put in the context.

Entry points: `bonsai-js` (environment, types, errors, `print`), `bonsai-js/service` (editor features), and `bonsai-js/query` (SQL and MongoDB translation). ESM only, zero dependencies. 1.0 is in release candidate: install `bonsai-js@next` (plain `bonsai-js` is 0.5.0 until 1.0.0). Runtimes: Node.js 22+, current Bun, modern ESM browsers.

## Quick start

```ts
import { bonsai, fn, t } from 'bonsai-js'

const env = bonsai({
  variables: {
    customer: t.object({ tier: t.enum('standard', 'gold'), email: t.optional(t.string()) }),
    cart: t.object({ items: t.list(t.object({ price: t.number(), qty: t.number() })) }),
  },
})

env.check('customer.teir == "gold"').ok // false: UNKNOWN_PROPERTY, did you mean "tier"?
const freeShipping = env.compile('customer.tier == "gold" || cart.items.map(.price * .qty).sum() >= 50', {
  expect: t.boolean(),
})
freeShipping.evaluateSync({ customer: { tier: 'standard' }, cart: { items: [{ price: 20, qty: 3 }] } }) // true
env.evaluateSync('customer.email ?? "no email"', ctx) // one-off evaluation, compiled once and cached
```

## Values

- `null`: the single absent value. Missing properties, missing variables, and host `undefined` read as `null`.
- boolean, number (IEEE-754 double; NaN/Infinity results are errors), string (UTF-16; `length` counts code units).
- list (host arrays, read by index, never mutated), map (plain objects and class instances via own properties; object literals). A value may have more keys than its declared type lists. Keys follow JavaScript property order: integer-like keys first, ascending, then insertion order.
- timestamp (a host `Date`, `now()`, `timestamp("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")`), duration (`days(3)`, `t1 - t2`).
- Opaque: functions, symbols, bigints, and built-in host objects (`Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet`, `RegExp`, promises, `ArrayBuffer` and typed arrays, errors, boxed primitives). Comparable with `==` and passable to host functions; reading a property is a `TYPE_ERROR`.
- `type(x)` returns "null", "boolean", "number", "string", "list", "map", "timestamp", "duration", or "opaque".

## Syntax

- Literals: `42`, `3.14`, `1e-3`, `1_000`, `0xff`, `0xde_ad`, `0b101`, `0o17` (a number starts with a digit: `.5` is invalid), `"text"`, `'text'`, `true`, `false`, `null`, `[1, ...rest]`, `{ a: 1, "b-c": 2, [key]: 3, ...other, name }`.
- Comments: `// line` and `/* block */`.
- Templates: `` `Hello ${name}` ``. `null` renders as empty text, timestamps and durations as ISO-8601, lists and maps are a type error.
- Reserved: `true false null let in not`. `has(...)` and `try(...)` are special forms. `|>` is reserved and is a syntax error.

## Operators (loosest to tightest)

1. `let x = e; body`
2. `c ? a : b` (right-associative)
3. `??`
4. `||`
5. `&&`
6. `==` `!=` (do not chain)
7. `<` `<=` `>` `>=` `in` `not in` (do not chain)
8. `+` `-`
9. `*` `/` `%`
10. `**` (right-associative)
11. prefix `!` `-`
12. `.` `?.` `[]` `?.[]` calls

Syntax errors instead of silent groupings: `??` mixed with `&&`/`||` without parentheses, `-x ** 2`, `a < b < c`, `a == b == c`.

- Equality: by value, no coercion. `1 == "1"` false; `[1, [2]] == [1, [2]]` true; maps compare by keys and values in any order; timestamps by instant; different kinds are unequal (never an error). `x == null` is true for missing or null.
- Ordering: two numbers, two strings, two timestamps, or two durations. If either side is `null` the result is `false` (so `users.filter(.age >= 18)` skips users without an age). Other mixes are type errors.
- Arithmetic: `+` on numbers, strings, lists, durations; timestamp +/- duration; timestamp - timestamp = duration; duration * or / number; duration / duration = number. No other combination: `null + 1`, `"a" + 1`, `t + 30` are errors. Division by zero is an error.
- Logic: `!`, `&&`, `||`, `?:` accept booleans and `null` (false); anything else is a type error. `&&`/`||` short-circuit and return booleans. `a ?? b` evaluates `b` only when `a` is `null`.
- Membership: `x in list` (by `==`), `"sub" in "string"`, `"key" in map`, `x in null` is false, `x not in y`.

## Property access

- `a.b` reads an own property of a map; missing is `null`; any property of `null` is `null`. Strings and lists have only `length`; other reads on non-maps are type errors.
- `a[k]`: string keys on maps (numbers become decimal text), integer indices on lists and strings (out of range, negative, or fractional is `null`; use `at(-1)`), `null` receiver or key gives `null`.
- `?.` equals `.` for reads. For calls it makes that one call return `null` when the receiver is `null`; it does not skip the rest of the chain: write `a?.trim()?.toUpperCase()`.
- Calling a function with `null` as the first argument, when no overload accepts null, is a `NULL_RECEIVER` error.
- `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype` are never data: not valid literal keys, a computed read is `null`, and writing one as a computed key is `BLOCKED_PROPERTY`.
- `has(a.b)` / `has(a[k])`: whether the own key (or list index) exists, even if the value is `null`.

## Functions and lambdas

- One namespace: `f(x, a)` and `x.f(a)` are the same call. `f` always resolves to a built-in or declared host function, never to a value in data.
- Built-ins are overloaded on parameter types; the overload is chosen statically when types are known, otherwise by runtime kinds.
- A host function with a built-in's name replaces it in that environment.
- Lambdas are arguments for function parameters only: `users.filter(u => u.age >= 18)`, `orders.map((o, i) => ...)`.
- Implicit `.`: `users.filter(.age >= 18 && !.suspended)`, `xs.map(. * 2)`, `rows.map(.[0])`. `.` binds to the nearest enclosing argument whose parameter is a function, skipping ordinary parameters: `users.filter(.score > max(.bonus, 10))` compares each user's own fields; `groups.map(.users.filter(.active).length)`.
- `.` directly inside an explicit lambda body is an error; name the outer item: `orders.filter(o => o.lines.some(.sku == o.promoSku))`.
- Higher-order functions call lambdas in order and stop early when the result is known.

## let, try, has

- `let total = items.map(.price * .qty).sum(); total > 100 ? total * 0.9 : total`. Bindings may shadow context variables, not other bindings.
- `try(expr, fallback)` catches evaluation errors (type errors, invalid arguments, division by zero, host functions that throw), never syntax, check, or limit errors, and never `HOST_CONTRACT`.

## Time

Timestamps are instants; durations are exact, in whole milliseconds (a day is 24 hours; a fraction of a millisecond rounds, halves away from zero). Calendar functions take an optional time zone, "UTC" or an IANA Area/Location name in the tz database spelling (abbreviations like "EST", other spellings like "utc", and offsets like "+05:30" are INVALID_ARGUMENT), and default to UTC: `year(t, tz)`, `startOfDay(t, tz)`, `addMonths(t, 1, tz)`, `formatDate(t, pattern, tz)`. `now()` is read once per evaluation, from the `now` evaluation option when given, otherwise from the environment clock. `addDays` keeps wall-clock time across DST; `+ days(n)` keeps exact length.

## Static checking

Gradual: unknown values are `any` (open environments, undeclared variables in non-strict environments, open records, and `values()`/`entries()`/computed reads on declared objects, which may carry extra keys). Declaring `variables` makes an environment strict unless `strict: false`. Errors: `UNKNOWN_VARIABLE` (strict), `UNKNOWN_PROPERTY` (closed records and map literals), `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`, `NO_OVERLOAD`, `TYPE_ERROR`, `NULLABLE_RECEIVER`, `INVALID_LAMBDA`, `BLOCKED_PROPERTY`, `EXPECTED_TYPE`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, plus `SYNTAX` and `LIMIT` from `check()`. Warnings (severity "warning"): `ALWAYS_FALSE` (comparisons that can never hold), `ALWAYS_TRUE` (`!=` or `not in` that always holds), `MAYBE_NULL` (a possibly-null value under `!`, `&&`, `||`, as a `?:` condition, or returned by a lambda where a boolean is expected; an ordering with a possibly-null side only where it is written so its false becomes a verdict: under `!`, as a `?:` test, in `every`/`none`, or compared with `false`, looking through `?:` branches, `let` bodies, `try`, and `== true`; a heuristic, so equivalent forms such as `!xs.some(...)` are not flagged), `NEVER_NULL` (`??` on never-null values), `UNSAFE_INTEGER` (number literals past 2^53 that cannot keep the digits written; `9007199254740993e0` is flagged, `1e308` is not).

## API

### bonsai(options) -> Environment

Options: `variables` (Record of types), `strict` (undeclared variables are errors; default true when `variables` is given), `functions` (host functions), `libraries` (`{ name, functions?, variables? }[]`, duplicate names are errors), `limits`, `cacheSize` (compiled programs cached, default 256), `clock` (`() => Date`), `validateContext` (check the context against declared types before each evaluation; fails with `INVALID_CONTEXT`).

Environment members:
- `check(src, { expect? })` -> `{ ok, type, diagnostics }`; never throws.
- `compile(src, { expect? })` -> Program; throws `BonsaiSyntaxError`, `BonsaiCheckError`, `BonsaiLimitError`.
- `evaluateSync(src, ctx?, options?)`, `evaluate(src, ctx?, options?)`: compile through an LRU cache (`cacheSize`, default 256) and evaluate.
- `explainSync(src, ctx?, options?)`, `explain(src, ctx?, options?)`: compile through the cache and explain (see Program).
- `extend(options)` -> new environment with more variables/functions/libraries.
- `listFunctions()`, `describeFunction(name)` -> `{ name, description, host, async, call, cost?, signatures: [{ params, required, rest?, returns }] }` (`call` for host functions declared `call: true`; `cost` when a host function declares one).
- `parse(src)` -> syntax tree; `variables`; `strict`.

Evaluation options: `timeout` (ms), `maxSteps`, `signal` (AbortSignal), `now` (Date: the time `now()` returns in this evaluation). `compile(src, { expect })` is cached: the same source and expected type return the same program. `env.partial(src, known, options?)` compiles through the cache and partially evaluates.

### Program

`source`, `ast`, `type`, `async`, `warnings`, `references: { variables, functions }`, `evaluate(ctx?, options?)`, `evaluateSync(ctx?, options?)`, `explain(ctx?, options?)`, `explainSync(ctx?, options?)`, `partial(known, options?)`. Results are plain values; timestamps are `Date`; durations are `Duration` (`ms`, ISO `toString()`).

### Explain

`await program.explain(ctx, options?)` (async, like `evaluate`) or `program.explainSync(ctx, options?)` evaluates and records every sub-expression's value. Returns `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error }` plus `trace` (nodes with `id`, `kind`, `text`, `start`, `end`, `value` or `error`, `children`, `evaluated: false` for skipped parts, `iterations` for lambda runs), `truncated`, `reasons()` (the conditions that decided the result), `toString()` (indented tree), and `toJSON()` (bounded snapshot that never runs getters). Evaluation errors are returned, not thrown. Options: the evaluation options plus `maxIterations` (default 20), `maxTraceNodes` (default 10000), `exhaustive` (also evaluate skipped `&&`/`||` sides so `reasons()` lists every failing condition).

### Partial evaluation

`program.partial(known, options?)` (synchronous) evaluates what `known` decides. Options: `unknown` (variables or dotted paths; without it, everything not given is unknown: a variable missing from `known`, a field missing from a known object, and a known object read whole; with it, only the listed paths are unknown and other missing data reads as null), `callHostFunctions` (default false), `now` (the time `now()` returns; otherwise `now()` stays in the residual), `maxSteps`, `timeout`, `signal` (one budget for the whole partial evaluation). Returns `{ status: 'value', value }`, `{ status: 'error', error }` (fails whatever the unknown data is), or `{ status: 'residual', residual, source, bindings, dependsOn, hostFunctions, readsContext, async, type, evaluate(ctx, options?), evaluateSync(ctx, options?), explain(ctx, options?), explainSync(ctx, options?) }`. The residual is exact: evaluating it with the full context gives the same value or error as the original. When `readsContext` is false, a context holding `dependsOn` is enough; when it is true (a `call: true` host function remains), pass the full context, known values included, since a missing known variable is `INVALID_CONTEXT`. Known values that are not short primitives are referenced as `__knownN` bindings (your own objects, not copies: do not mutate `known` afterwards); `evaluate`/`evaluateSync` supply them. With `validateContext`, `partial()` validates the known variables and a residual validates what it reads (pass `validateContext: false` per evaluation for a context validated upstream).

### Query translation (bonsai-js/query)

`toSQL(program, { row, columns, dialect, known?, now?, maxSteps?, timeout?, signal?, callHostFunctions?, paramOffset? })` -> `{ sql, params }` for Postgres or SQLite; `toMongo(program, { row, fields, known?, now?, maxSteps?, timeout?, signal?, callHostFunctions? })` -> `{ filter, options }` (pass `options` to `find()`). `program` is a compiled program (not a partial-evaluation residual; anything else is a `TypeError`). `row` names the record variable; every other variable must be in `known`, and a path the filter reads must be present in its known value (missing is `UNTRANSLATABLE`, not null, unless that read is guarded by `??`, a `== null` test, or a `has(p) &&` branch; `let` names are followed to their paths); in a typed environment a known object read whole (spread, `keys()`/`values()`, `==`, passed on) must have every declared field. `maxSteps` (default 1,000,000), `timeout`, and `signal` bound the whole translation, including writing known lists and text into the query; in SQL a known value is sent once however often it is used. `callHostFunctions: true` calls sync host functions with known inputs before translating (as `partial()` does), e.g. to list the records an authorization policy allows for a known subject. Columns map keys to `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `timestamp`, `duration` (whole milliseconds; or `{ type, name }`); anything else is rejected; when the program's environment declares a type for a field, a column of a different type (a list field declared `text`) is a `TypeError`. The query selects exactly the records for which the filter is `true` in Bonsai. Translates comparisons, `&&`/`||`/`!`, `in` known lists, boolean columns, `startsWith`/`endsWith`/`includes` on text columns (also `x?.f(k) ?? false`, `x?.f(k) == true`, and `(x ?? "").f(k)`), a column with a known default (`(order.total ?? 0) >= 500`), duration columns and `inMilliseconds(col)` (SQL; `?.` form also MongoDB), arithmetic (SQL), and relative dates (`now() - order.placed < days(14)`, `order.placed + days(3) > now()`). Parts without an exact database equivalent throw `BonsaiTranslationError` (`UNTRANSLATABLE`) with the span and a reason (missing `now` option, calendar functions, `let`, `?:`, `try()`). A misspelled row, known value, or column names the closest match. Unknown options are `TypeError`s.

### Syntax trees

`env.parse(src)` returns a JSON syntax tree (`type`, `start`, `end` on every node; a parenthesized node includes its parentheses); the standalone `parse(src, limits?)` does the same without an environment (only the parse limits apply; the other `limits` keys are ignored). `print(tree, { calls?: 'method' | 'function' })` turns a tree back into source that evaluates the same way. `forEachChild(node, visit)` visits a node's children in evaluation order, and `mapChildren(node, rewrite)` returns a copy with each child replaced by `rewrite(child)`.

### Host functions

```ts
fn({
  params: [t.string(), t.optional(t.number())],
  required: 1, // later parameters are optional, must be nullable, and arrive as null when omitted
  rest: t.number(), // optional variadic type
  returns: t.boolean(),
  async: false, // true: run returns a promise; evaluateSync rejects the expression with ASYNC_IN_SYNC; a promise from a non-async function is HOST_CONTRACT
  call: false, // true: run(call, ...args), call = { context, signal }; signal aborts when the evaluation times out or is cancelled while waiting
  description: 'Shown in listFunctions and editor hovers',
  cost: 32, // steps charged per call (default 32); lower for cheap pure helpers
  run: (name, count) => true,
})
```

Arguments are validated before `run`; results are checked deeply against `returns` (`HOST_CONTRACT` otherwise, not caught by `try`); exceptions (even a `BonsaiError`) become `HOST_ERROR` with `cause`. `withContext<Ctx>()` returns an `fn` variant whose `run` receives the call with `call.context` typed. Libraries: `{ name, functions, variables } satisfies Library`; their variables join the environment's context type.

### Types (t)

`t.string()`, `t.number()`, `t.boolean()`, `t.null()`, `t.timestamp()`, `t.duration()`, `t.literal(v)`, `t.enum(...values)`, `t.list(T)`, `t.object({ ... })` (closed), `t.record(V)` (open; reads are `V | null`), `t.optional(T)` (`T | null`, also optional key), `t.union(...)`, `t.opaque(name)`, `t.any()`, `t.never()`. `Infer<typeof T>` gives the TypeScript type. `formatType(type)`, `isAssignable(source, target)`. Types are JSON-serializable.

### Errors

All errors from checking and evaluating extend `BonsaiError` with `name` (the class name, kept when minified), `code`, `source`, `span` (`{ start, end }`), `position` (1-based), `formatted` (message + code frame); diagnostics (`check().diagnostics`, `BonsaiCheckError.diagnostics`, `program.warnings`) carry `code`, `message`, `severity`, `start`, `end`, `span`, `position`, `formatted`, and `suggestion` (the name to use instead, for unknown names); `check()` also returns `ast` (the checked tree), `typeOf(node)`, and, when ok, `program` (compiled on first read); exceptions from host code (functions, getters, Proxies, including a `BonsaiError` a host function throws) are wrapped as `HOST_ERROR`. `isBonsaiError(value)` recognizes a Bonsai error, also one from another copy of the package. Error constructors are not public API. Invalid configuration throws `TypeError` or `RangeError` (a wrong type or unknown option key is a `TypeError`, a value out of range a `RangeError`) from `bonsai()`, `fn()`, `compile()`/`check()`, `evaluate*()` and `explain*()` (per-evaluation options, or a context that is not an object), `partial()`, `toSQL()`/`toMongo()`, and `print()` (trees the parser could not produce).
- `BonsaiSyntaxError`: `SYNTAX`
- `BonsaiCheckError`: `CHECK` (`.diagnostics`)
- `BonsaiLimitError`: `SOURCE_TOO_LONG`, `TOO_DEEP` (syntax), `TOO_MANY_NODES`, `TOO_COMPLEX`, `STEP_LIMIT`, `STRING_LIMIT`, `LIST_LIMIT`, `VALUE_DEPTH_LIMIT` (nested data), `PATTERN_LIMIT`, `TIMEOUT`, `ABORTED`; `.limit` names the option to raise (`maxSteps`, `timeout`, `signal`, ...; undefined for fixed bounds and for a call stack overflow)
- `BonsaiTranslationError` (from `bonsai-js/query`): `UNTRANSLATABLE`
- `BonsaiRuntimeError`: `TYPE_ERROR`, `NO_OVERLOAD`, `NULL_RECEIVER`, `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`, `NON_FINITE`, `BLOCKED_PROPERTY`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `ASYNC_IN_SYNC`, `HOST_ERROR`, `HOST_CONTRACT`, `INVALID_CONTEXT`

### Limits (defaults)

`maxSourceLength` 100000, `maxDepth` 128, `maxNodes` 20000, `maxSteps` 1000000 (0 disables; charged by the real cost of each operation, deterministic), `maxStringLength` 100000, `maxListLength` 100000, `maxValueDepth` 64 (values built or walked), `maxPatternLength` 4096 (regex patterns, `PATTERN_LIMIT`), `timeout` 0 (none). Each host call costs its function's `cost` (default 32 steps).

### Language service (bonsai-js/service)

`createLanguageService(env, { expect? })` (expect adds EXPECTED_TYPE to diagnostics) -> `{ complete(src, offset), hover(src, offset), diagnostics(src) }`. `complete` returns `{ start, end, items: [{ label, kind, detail, documentation?, insertText, range? }] }` with kinds `value`, `variable`, `local`, `property`, `function`, `method`, `keyword`. It never evaluates or calls host functions.

## Security model

Expression text is untrusted; context data and host functions are trusted. Expressions cannot run code, reach prototypes or globals, call functions found in data, trigger conversion hooks, mutate data, or run unbounded: the step budget charges every operation for its real cost, including text search, regular expressions, sorting, and time zone math. Built-ins never run host code on receivers (no iterators, species, or methods). Host functions run with full privileges and cannot be interrupted while running synchronously; getters and Proxies in the context run when read. Declared types are not access control: `keys()`, `values()`, `entries()`, and dynamic indexing read every own enumerable property of the data passed in.

## Migrating from 0.x

`a |> f(b)` -> `a.f(b)`; `upper`/`lower` -> `toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase`; `flatten` -> `flat`; stdlib plugins -> built in; `addFunction` -> `functions: { name: fn({...}) }`; `addContextFunction` -> `fn({ call: true, run: (call, ...args) => ... })` reading `call.context`; `validate()` -> `check()`; `evaluateExpression` -> `bonsai().evaluateSync`; `allowedProperties` -> pass only the data expressions may read; `x == null` now includes missing values; `&&`/`||` are strict booleans (use `??` for defaults). Results that changed silently: `round` rounds halves away from zero and honors digits; `avg([])` is null; `unique` compares by value; templates render null as empty text and dates as ISO-8601; `toNumber` of invalid text is an error; division and remainder by zero are errors; `sort()` is numeric; `includes`/`indexOf`/`in` and `Date` equality compare by value; `replace` inserts its replacement literally; `substring` -> `slice` and `charAt` -> `at` differ for reversed or negative positions. Requires Node.js 22+. Full guide: https://danfry1.github.io/bonsai-js/guide/migrating

## Stability

Semantic Versioning covers the language (an expression that evaluates successfully keeps its result) and the exported API, including error codes and error JSON. A minor release may add syntax, functions, optional option fields, result fields, and union variants (avoid exhaustive switches without a default), change messages and step costs, and simplify residuals. Not public: error constructors, host functions not built with `fn()`, and implementing `Environment`, `Program`, `Explanation`, `Trace`, or `LanguageService` yourself. The result type parameter of `env.evaluate<R>()` and similar is an unchecked assertion; use `compile(src, { expect })` for a checked type. Full policy: https://danfry1.github.io/bonsai-js/guide/stability

## Built-in functions

Every built-in is callable as `f(x, ...)` or `x.f(...)`. `?` marks an optional parameter.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED FUNCTIONS -->

### Text

- toUpperCase(string): string: Upper-cases text.
- toLowerCase(string): string: Lower-cases text.
- trim(string): string: Removes leading and trailing whitespace.
- trimStart(string): string: Removes leading whitespace.
- trimEnd(string): string: Removes trailing whitespace.
- startsWith(string, string): boolean: Whether text starts with a prefix.
- endsWith(string, string): boolean: Whether text ends with a suffix.
- includes(string, string): boolean: Whether text contains a substring, or a list contains a value.
- indexOf(string, string): number: Position of the first match, or -1.
- lastIndexOf(string, string): number: Position of the last match, or -1.
- slice(string, number, number?): string: A section of text or a list; negative positions count from the end.
- split(string, string, number?): string[]: Splits text on a separator.
- replace(string, string, string): string: Replaces the first occurrence of some text (no patterns).
- replaceAll(string, string, string): string: Replaces every occurrence of some text (no patterns).
- padStart(string, number, string?): string: Pads text at the start to a length.
- padEnd(string, number, string?): string: Pads text at the end to a length.
- repeat(string, number): string: Repeats text a number of times.
- at(string, number): string | null: The item or character at a position; negative positions count from the end.
- matches(string, string): boolean: Whether text contains a match for a regular expression (JavaScript syntax without backreferences or lookaround, linear time; anchor with ^ and $; prefix (?i) to ignore case).
- toString(string | number | boolean | null | timestamp | duration): string: Renders a value as text, as a template would.
- toNumber(string | number): number: Parses decimal text as a number, e.g. "-12.5" or "1e3" (surrounding whitespace is ignored; 0x and other bases are not accepted).

### Lists

- map(T[], (T, number) => U): U[]: Transforms each item.
- filter(T[], (T, number) => boolean): T[]: Keeps the items for which the lambda is true.
- find(T[], (T, number) => boolean): T | null: The first item for which the lambda is true, or null.
- findIndex(T[], (T, number) => boolean): number: The position of the first item for which the lambda is true, or -1.
- some(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean: Whether the lambda is true for at least one item.
- every(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean: Whether the lambda is true for every item.
- none(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean: Whether the lambda is false for every item.
- count(T[]): number; count(T[], (T, number) => boolean): number: The number of items, or of items for which the lambda is true.
- flatMap(T[], (T, number) => U[] | U): U[]: Transforms each item and flattens list results one level.
- reduce(T[], (U, T) => U, U): U: Folds a list into one value: reduce(list, (acc, item) => ..., initial). Name both parameters; "." is not allowed, since the first one is the accumulator.
- sort(T[], ("asc" | "desc")?): T[]: Sorts numbers, text, timestamps, or durations; pass "desc" to reverse.
- sortBy(T[], (T, number) => K, ("asc" | "desc")?): T[]: Sorts by a key; pass "desc" to reverse. Nulls sort first ("asc") or last ("desc").
- groupBy(T[], (T, number) => string | number | boolean): { [key: string]: T[] }: Groups items into a map of lists by a key. Map keys are text, so a key is its text form: 1 and "1", or true and "true", share a group. A key must be a string, number, or boolean (null is an error). Keys are listed integer-like first, ascending, then in first-seen order.
- reverse(T[]): T[]: The items in reverse order.
- unique(T[]): T[]: The items without duplicates (by value), in first-seen order.
- flat(any[]): any[]: Flattens nested lists one level.
- first(T[]): T | null: The first item, or null.
- last(T[]): T | null: The last item, or null.
- join((string | number | boolean | null | timestamp | duration)[], string?): string: Joins items into text with a separator (default ",").
- slice(T[], number, number?): T[]: A section of text or a list; negative positions count from the end.
- at(T[], number): T | null: The item or character at a position; negative positions count from the end.
- includes(T[], any): boolean: Whether text contains a substring, or a list contains a value.

### Time

- now(): timestamp: The current time, fixed for one evaluation.
- timestamp(string): timestamp; timestamp(number): timestamp; timestamp(timestamp): timestamp: Parses ISO-8601 text (years 0000-9999, or six digits with a sign such as +012345, as a timestamp renders) or epoch milliseconds (a fraction is dropped toward zero, as Date does) into a timestamp.
- duration(string): duration; duration(duration): duration: Parses ISO-8601 duration text in weeks, days, hours, minutes, and seconds (e.g. "PT1H30M", "-P2DT0.5S"), the text a duration renders as.
- weeks(number): duration: A duration of n weeks.
- days(number): duration: A duration of n days (24 hours each).
- hours(number): duration: A duration of n hours.
- minutes(number): duration: A duration of n minutes.
- seconds(number): duration: A duration of n seconds.
- milliseconds(number): duration: A duration of n milliseconds. Durations are whole milliseconds: a fraction rounds to the nearest one, halves away from zero.
- inDays(duration): number: A duration as a (fractional) number of days.
- inHours(duration): number: A duration as a number of hours.
- inMinutes(duration): number: A duration as a number of minutes.
- inSeconds(duration): number: A duration as a number of seconds.
- inMilliseconds(duration): number: A duration as a number of milliseconds.
- year(timestamp, string?): number: The calendar year, in a time zone (default UTC).
- month(timestamp, string?): number: The month 1-12, in a time zone (default UTC).
- day(timestamp, string?): number: The day of the month, in a time zone (default UTC).
- hour(timestamp, string?): number: The hour 0-23, in a time zone (default UTC).
- minute(timestamp, string?): number: The minute, in a time zone (default UTC).
- second(timestamp, string?): number: The second, in a time zone (default UTC).
- dayOfWeek(timestamp, string?): number: The ISO weekday (Monday 1 to Sunday 7), in a time zone (default UTC).
- startOfDay(timestamp, string?): timestamp: Midnight at the start of the day, in a time zone (default UTC).
- startOfMonth(timestamp, string?): timestamp: Midnight on the first of the month, in a time zone (default UTC).
- startOfYear(timestamp, string?): timestamp: Midnight on January 1, in a time zone (default UTC).
- addDays(timestamp, number, string?): timestamp: Adds calendar days (keeps the wall-clock time across DST), in a time zone.
- addMonths(timestamp, number, string?): timestamp: Adds calendar months, clamping the day to the month length.
- addYears(timestamp, number, string?): timestamp: Adds calendar years (Feb 29 becomes Feb 28).
- formatDate(timestamp, string, string?): string: Formats a timestamp in a time zone (default UTC). Tokens: yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h a mm m ss s SSS; quote literal text ('at'), and write '' for a quote ('it''s').
- abs(duration): duration: Absolute value.
- sum((duration | null)[]): duration: The sum of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped), added left to right as a + b + c is.
